messages:
Maria (CS): Quick heads-up — Acme is asking for a formal SLA/SLO extract for their renewal pack. They want clarity on uptime % and latency targets, plus how credits would be calculated if we miss the SLA. Can someone assemble a short customer-facing summary?

Ajay (SE): I can draft the latency SLO section and share a dashboard link. Do we have agreed numbers for p95/p99 for hosted API?

Lucas (SRE): Our current internal SLOs (hosted-prod) are: uptime 99.9% monthly, p95 latency <250ms, p99 latency <800ms. I can validate last 90 days of metrics. :eyes:

Maria (CS): perfect — can you also confirm last month's actuals? Acme will want the month-on-month view for billing/credits. They flagged a 45m incident two weeks ago as a concern.

Lucas (SRE): Confirmed we have the incident on record — post-mortem shows a model rollout OOM that caused degraded routing for 45 minutes on 2025-11-12 (see incident-20251112). Last month overall uptime = 99.86% (so under 99.9%). p95 = 230ms, p99 = 710ms.

Rachel (AM): If uptime falls below 99.9% for the month, the contract says credits pro-rated by downtime. Does billing-bot have the formula we use?

billing-bot: Standard credit calc: credit = (downtime_minutes / total_minutes_in_billing_period) * monthly_fee. See internal KB: https://redwood.internal/kb/sla-credit-policy

Maria (CS): do we want to offer Acme a one-off goodwill credit for that incident to smooth renewal, or stick strictly to contract terms? They hinted pretty strongly during the CSAT call.

Ajay (SE): If we provide the customer-facing SLO page and the metrics (99.86% last month + incident details), we can propose a one-time 5% service credit as a gesture. That buys goodwill without opening precedent. :+1:

Lucas (SRE): From ops side, fine. I'll produce a short metrics export: a CSV with daily uptime and p95/p99 for the last 3 months. Also will attach the incident timeline and mitigations (what we fixed in the rollout pipeline).

Maria (CS): that works. Draft ask for Acme: include the SLO table (below), a short explanation of credit calc, and the incident note. Please make it < 1 page.

Ajay (SE): SLO table snippet to include (will format for the doc):

```
SLO | Target | Last 30d actual
Uptime (monthly) | 99.9% | 99.86%
Latency p95 | <250 ms | 230 ms
Latency p99 | <800 ms | 710 ms
```

Maria (CS): Nice. Rachel, can you confirm billing contact and draft the credits line for the customer-facing note? We should avoid legal phrasing but remain contract-accurate.

Rachel (AM): Billing contact is billing@acme.inc. For customer note: "If monthly uptime falls below 99.9%, Acme will be eligible for a service credit calculated as (downtime_minutes / total_minutes_in_billing_period) * monthly_fee. For this specific event, our recommended one-time goodwill credit is 5% of the last invoice." I'll CC billing and legal on the final.

Lucas (SRE): Uploaded CSV + incident timeline to the shared folder: https://redwood.internal/shares/acme/sla-exports/2025-11. I'll also add a short blurb about the rollout fix and the guarded rollout flag we added.

Maria (CS): Great — action items: Lucas: export and timeline (ETA today EOD). Ajay: one-page SLO doc + dashboard share (ETA tomorrow AM). Rachel: draft credit wording and loop in billing/legal (ETA tomorrow AM). I'll own the customer touchpoint and send final note after reviews. :thumbsup:

Ajay (SE): I'll also create a temporary dashboard with view-only link for Acme showing the 30/90 day trends. Link will go in the doc.

Maria (CS): Thanks team. I'll post the customer note here before sending so we can review tone.

Rachel (AM): One more thing — please include the remediation timeline in the note (what we did and what prevents recurrence). Customers care about root cause + fix.

Lucas (SRE): will do. Also flag: if Acme asks for historical credits beyond that month, we should route to legal. This one-off is fine.

Maria (CS): noted. Closing loop once docs are in. :white_check_mark:
